summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of recurrent pancreatitis was admitted due to a relapse of severe right epigastric pain shortly after discharge from a prior hospitalization. She was initially kept NPO and managed with IV fluids and a hydromorphone PCA for pain control. Imaging with MRCP showed chronic changes consistent with prior pancreatitis but no acute complications. A PICC line was placed for fluid and medication access, later replaced due to poor flow. Parenteral nutrition was initiated to support nutritional recovery. Her pain improved, allowing transition to oral medications and gradual advancement of diet. Diarrhea was attributed to a new bowel regimen, with negative C. difficile testing. She was discharged home in improved condition with a plan for oral pain management, GI follow-up, and continuation of psychiatric medications.
